text: Child support formulas don't aim to reproduce exactly what each child would need, but they're supposed to approximate the child's share of the family budget while the parents were together. And so they factor in incomes and number of kids and their age, etc. So income is a proxy for what each family will need. But nothing in law is perfect. You can argue for upping the support of kids that need a lot of money, say a medical condition, etc. That's what deviation motions are for. People tend to use these guidelines because they're neutral. By neutral I mean that parents can't game the formula (or rather not easily). If the amount is based on individual subjective needs of each child, then one parent will always argue for a lot more while the other argues for a lot less. And that's what guideline formulas are trying to avoid.
